name: Boat Safety Checklist
description: A pre-departure safety routine covering life jackets, signaling devices, communication, weather and a float plan before heading out on the water.

items.text: Carry a properly fitting life jacket for every person aboard
Include correctly sized life jackets for children
Have a throwable flotation device if required
Check life jackets for damage and working buckles
Wear life jackets in rough water and by children
Carry visual distress signals such as flares
items.note: Check expiry dates and regional requirements

items.text: Have a sound-producing device like a horn or whistle
Confirm navigation lights work for low light and night
Carry fire extinguishers, charged and within date
Keep a first aid kit stocked and accessible
Test the VHF radio and know the emergency channel
Carry a charged phone in a waterproof case as backup
Have charts or a GPS chartplotter for your area
Check the compass and confirm it reads correctly
Confirm you know local markers and no-go zones
Check the marine forecast before leaving
Note wind, wave height, tides and visibility
Watch for changing skies and storms while underway
Set a turn-back time and stick to it
Plan a route that suits the conditions and your boat
Write a float plan with route, crew and return time
Leave the float plan with a trusted person ashore
Brief passengers on life jacket and emergency locations
Explain how to call for help on the radio
Assign a second person who can operate the boat
Check fuel level and carry a reserve
Confirm the bilge pump works and bilge is clear
Test the engine and steering at the dock
Check the battery is charged and connections secure
Confirm anchor, line and fenders are aboard
Verify drain plug is installed before launching

faq.q: How many life jackets do I need on board?
faq.a: Most regions require a properly fitting, wearable life jacket for every person aboard, plus a throwable device on larger boats. Check sizes for children and confirm condition. Exact requirements vary by region, so follow your local Coast Guard or maritime rules.

faq.q: What safety equipment is legally required?
faq.a: Required gear typically includes life jackets, fire extinguishers, visual distress signals, a sound-producing device and navigation lights, but the exact list varies by region and vessel size. Verify the rules with your local Coast Guard or maritime authority before you depart.

faq.q: What is a float plan and why file one?
faq.a: A float plan is a written note of where you are going, who is aboard and when you expect to return, left with a trusted person ashore. If you do not return on time, they can alert authorities and speed up any search and rescue.

faq.q: How do I check the weather before boating?
faq.a: Review the marine forecast for wind, waves, storms and visibility before leaving and again while underway. Conditions can change fast on the water, so be ready to shorten the trip or return early if the forecast worsens.

faq.q: Can I print this boat safety checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it aboard and run through life jackets, signaling, communication, weather and your float plan before every trip.
